faq: What does this tool calculate?
The point's pixel position within its tile: world pixel modulo 256 in each axis, at the chosen zoom.
Which map standard does it use?
The slippy-map standard (Web Mercator, 256-px tiles) shared by OSM, Google and MapLibre.
Can I use this in production GIS?
The formulas are the production standard itself — yes for web-mapping work.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 — tile systems are defined over it.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — tiles and pixels quantise; decimals beyond the cell are decoration.
Tiles are 256 × 256 — the offset is an address inside that square, origin at the top-left (northwest) corner.
Y grows downward — really?
Screen convention: pixel y counts south from the tile's top. Latitude's northward growth flips at the world-pixel step, and this page inherits the flip faithfully.
Retina tiles (@2x)?
512-px tiles double the offset range (0–511) for the same ground — state your tile flavour when comparing values.
Offset for a tile centre?
(128, 128) by definition — the centre calculator's point has this page's most boring answer.
Sub-pixel precision?
World pixels are fractional before flooring; offsets can be reported fractionally for smooth rendering — integers serve tile addressing.
